entries.title: Shared/Core update: resource-limits

ai.title: CPU resource limits now allow Cloud chat restarts
ai.summary: The `CLOUD_RESTARTABLE_RESOURCES` constant in the `common` package now includes `'cpu'`, allowing web-based Cloud chats that hit a CPU limit to restart from their saved file copy instead of being permanently dead-ended. This change addresses an issue where ordinary builds stopped approximately 550 chats for good on November 25th because Agent 37 VM chats were restricted to a single CPU. The `CLOUD_RESOURCE_RESTARTS_PER_DAY` cap of 3 remains in effect to prevent sustained high-CPU usage, such as mining, from consuming Cloud resources indefinitely. The `cloudResourceRestarts` function will now return true for CPU trips, enabling the restart workflow for both web and Desktop clients.
ai.evidence: In `common/src/desktop-cloud/resource-limits.ts`, the `CLOUD_RESTARTABLE_RESOURCES` array is updated to include `'cpu'` alongside `'files'`, `'processes'`, and `'memory'`, with a comment explaining that CPU limits previously stopped chats permanently because Agent 37 VMs were held to one CPU.

eli5.text: The assistant can now restart your web-based cloud session if a task keeps the processor fully busy for over 30 seconds. This applies to users who use the web interface and prevents the chat from ending permanently when a build uses too much processing power. A limit of three restarts per day still applies to prevent continuous heavy usage, and a full storage drive still requires moving the session to the desktop app.
